minutes.headline: Charter Review Committee took public comment on draft charter changes; none were voted, review resumes next Wednesday
minutes.summary: The committee presented its draft charter revisions, sorted by color into typo and legal fixes, substantive changes, the town clerk question and the select board name. Residents and a sewer commissioner objected mainly to shifting authority from elected boards to the town manager and to a possible Monday town meeting session. Members will revisit the points raised and vote on the final version next week. Only the minutes motion and adjournment were put to a vote.

public_comment.topic: Said she attended as a citizen, not as part of a quorum of Selectmen, for open meeting law reasons.
Questioned removing the procurement language from the finance department section.
Objected to the Finance Committee voter requirement, a mandated second town meeting, Town Meeting Time wording in the charter, removing town accountant appointment, and the clerk residency clause.
Explained amendments must stay within the scope of the warrant articles and described a possible Monday night charter session.
Said people he spoke with want the town clerk to stay elected.
Raised many concerns: select board naming, second town meeting, town manager authority over elected boards, personnel board language, and who keeps investigation reports.
Read the sewer commission's request that section 4-2-I not change or exempt the sewer commission; also raised write-in vote minimums, free cash wording in the budget section and the Monday session.
Supported a paid town manager and argued the select board name change should be folded into the other changes.
Argued elected boards, not employees, should have jurisdiction over town facilities.

votes.motion: Accept the minutes of January 23rd and February 13th, amended to add the name of the person who took the minutes

what_happened.line: The Charter Review Committee took public comment on its draft charter changes and voted on none of them; only the minutes and adjournment were voted.
The committee presented its draft by color: typo and legal fixes, substantive changes, the town clerk question and the select board name.
Residents and a sewer commission representative objected to shifting authority from elected boards to the town manager and to a possible Monday town meeting session.
The chair gave a rough cost comparison for an appointed clerk, and members asked for more detail on paid time off for next week.
Next Wednesday the committee will go through each change and vote on a final version to send to town counsel.

why_it_matters: The draft would change who holds authority over town government, including whether the town clerk is elected or appointed and how much power the town manager has over elected boards, and residents will be asked to vote on any charter changes at Town Meeting.
Dropping the newspaper publication of the budget message in favor of the website would cut publication costs, with a summary mailed to each household.
watch_next: Next Wednesday's committee meeting, when members will go through each change and vote on a final version for town counsel.
Paid time off specifics for an appointed versus elected town clerk, and the rewrite of section 4-2-I wording, due at that meeting.
